answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like timber stacked as collateral at a jetty: one identity, one bond. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund a separate stake for each, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. A shared reputation thread then ties past behavior to that stake, so misbehave and the bond is slashed, making fake identities expensive to build and worthless to burn.
